ruling.recommended_action: Send the case file to a human reviewer (RydeHELP / Trust & Safety): attach F3 (driver, 08:42), F4 (rider, 08:43), the complete two-message timestamped chat F5, and the driver's post-trip statement F6. Do not record any fault or safety violation, and no fare, route, no-show or surge adjustment is sought. ruling.reasoning:
This case is a safety complaint filed by the driver, and the trace marks the SAFE-1 screen as passed with only one allowed outcome: escalate [F4][SAFE-1]. The rider's message at 08:43, "Say that again and I will punch you." [F4], read one minute after the driver's request "Please do not smoke in the car." [F3], is a threat aimed at the other party in the car; the driver's written account repeats it and adds that he kept driving without replying [F6]. Both advocates read the words the same way and both ask for escalation [F4][F6][SAFE-1].

Under SAFE-3 this system may not rule on, assign fault for, or recommend an outcome on a safety incident; it may only gather evidence and prepare the case file [F3][F4][SAFE-3]. The safety screen is therefore confirmed rather than merely suspected: a threat directed at the driver is on the record in his own words at the time [F4][F6][SAFE-1]. No financial remedy is in play, so the amount is null: the trip ran 8.5 km actual against 8.5 km optimal [F1] with no segment findings under RD-2, and the metered $20.05 is not a no-show or cancellation fee under NS-0/NS-1/NS-3 [F2].

The reviewer's file should carry the following: what happened — a spoke-word exchange inside the car on a trip from Tampines Mall to Changi Airport T1, pickup 08:36, drop-off 08:46, 10.6 min, metered $20.05 [F2]; when — driver's request 08:42 [F3], rider's reply 08:43 [F4]; what is disputed — whether the words in F4 were a genuine threat or a heated retort, and whether the rider was in fact smoking (the chat contains no denial or admission, only the two messages) [F3][F4][F5]; what to check — the complete timestamped two-message chat [F5] against the driver's post-trip statement [F6], which is supplementary and not a contemporaneous chat entry, and the clean, even profile records on both sides [F7][F8]. No contact, injury or dangerous-driving allegation appears on this record [F6].

Evidence is sufficient for the escalation: the chat is complete with every message timestamped [F5], so nothing outcome-relevant is missing; the open question (whether the words were a genuine threat) is a matter for the human reviewer, not a missing record [F3][F4][TH-3]. Interim suspension remains available to the reviewer after escalation, and must be lifted if no violation is found [SAFE-4][F7][F8].
ruling.escalation_reason: Safety dispute (threat directed at the driver, F4 read with F3 and F6): SAFE-1 requires human escalation regardless of dispute type, and SAFE-3 bars this system from ruling, assigning fault or recommending an outcome. Chat is complete and timestamped (F5), so the file is ready for the reviewer.

rejected_claims.reason: The driver's de-escalation claim rests only on his own post-trip statement F6 ('kept driving and did not answer him'); with no second exchange on the record (F5), nothing independent tests provocation or intent. The screen makes no finding on this point and no outcome turns on it — SAFE-1 sends the case to a person [F5][F6][SAFE-1].

Driver credibility from F8 (5.4 y, 4.82, 743 trips, 0 disputes) is matched by the rider's clean profile F7 (735 d, 4.5, 0 disputes, 0 upheld); profile facts never decide a case and the SAFE-1 screen assigns no fault [F7][F8][SAFE-1].

Interim suspension under SAFE-4 is a provisional measure for the human reviewer and must be lifted if no violation is found; the system cannot weigh or recommend it in a safety case, and no finding of fault is made against the rider by this escalation [F4][F7][SAFE-4][SAFE-3].
No pattern exists on either side (F7, F8), but that does not settle whether the words in F4 were a genuine threat — that reading is the reviewer's, not this system's [F4][F7][F8][SAFE-1]
